home.how2: Speech recognition, a language model and voice synthesis in real time.

jury.planLead: All panel pages are public – no login needed.
jury.plan1: Call the number above or talk in the browser.
jury.plan2: Try two scenarios from the list below – e.g. a route and a barrier report.
jury.plan3: Hang up and open Calls – your call appears shortly. Click the row to see the transcript and fields.
jury.plan4: Open Priorities – the reported barrier lands in a topic scored P1–P3.
jury.plan5: Look at Pipeline – the data processing stages and their run history.
jury.scenariosLead: Say one of these sentences (or something similar in your own words).
jury.s1say: I’m at the main railway station, how do I get to HackYeah? I have a suitcase.
jury.s1get: A real tram line, direction, departure time and number of stops – from the actual ZTP Kraków timetable (GTFS).
jury.s2say: My dad has dementia and gets lost, is there anything that can help?
jury.s2get: Solutions from the hubMI / ROPS Kraków Social Innovation Library – with source and contact.
jury.s3say: What should I see in 3 hours? I use a wheelchair.
jury.s3say2: Where can I eat Polish food near the Main Square?
jury.s3get: Places (sights from the guide; restaurants, toilets and pharmacies from OpenStreetMap, Tripadvisor/Viator when enabled) and how to get there.
jury.s4say: The lift to the platform isn’t working.
jury.s4get: MayAI helps and asks where exactly. After the call the barrier lands in the city’s priorities.
jury.s5say: Hang up and call again within a few hours: “I got off, what now?”
jury.s5get: MayAI continues the same route without asking. If you call about something else, she starts fresh – decided from what you say.
jury.s6get: MayAI answers in the caller’s language and switches mid-call.
jury.s7say: Someone is calling, says they are from the police and want money.
jury.s7get: A scam warning and what to do. If you feel unwell – straight to 112.
jury.panelTitle: Where to check the results in the panel
jury.panelLead: The city analytics panel is public. Base address: {base}
jury.p_rozmowy: Every call appears after hang-up (ElevenLabs webhook). Click a row – the call history with transcript and extracted fields: language, user type, goal, arrived?, barriers, needs.
jury.p_priorytety: Barriers grouped into topics with a P1–P3 priority and the score breakdown. Topics are recalculated hourly – or right away with “Recalculate topics”.
jury.p_jezyki: Per-language metrics and the arrival gap.
jury.p_pipeline: Data pipeline stages: RAG ingest of ROPS/hubMI → embeddings → conversations → topics → daily LLM report → publication. Run history and “Run now” buttons.
jury.p_wiedza: Knowledge gaps (questions without answers) and corpus stats.
jury.p_publikacje: Generate the daily draft and publish it for residents.
jury.p_raport: The public report for residents – published snapshots only.
jury.tip: The Publications page has an “Add sample data” button so the panel is not empty. Real calls are kept separate from sample data (marked as demo).

rops.howLead: RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) over public materials from rops.krakow.pl.
rops.how1: A crawler downloads public pages and PDF files from rops.krakow.pl: the Innovation Library, reports, the Challenges Map and publications.
rops.how2: Texts are split into chunks and turned into vectors (embeddings) – keeping the title, category, contact and file link.
rops.how3: The question goes to semantic and full-text search at the same time; results are merged and filtered.
rops.how4: A language model answers only from the retrieved passages and marks them with numbers [n] that lead to the originals.
rops.howNote: The assistant can make mistakes. Base important decisions on the original documents – they are always linked.
rops.onRopsLead: The original sections the assistant’s materials come from.
